findings: The exact repository source only asks for a non-recursive binary-tree traversal implementation; it does not identify a traversal order or prescribe a node/API contract.
The candidate makes its broader coverage explicit by treating preorder, inorder and postorder plus null/API semantics as answer-side choices rather than recovered source requirements.

Preorder correctly exploits LIFO ordering by pushing the right child before the left child; inorder explicitly stores the pending ancestor chain; postorder uses node identity in lastVisited to distinguish an unvisited right subtree from a completed one.
The postorder implementation is safe for duplicate node values because traversal state compares node references, not values.

Independent validation compiles the actual candidate and compares all three traversal orders with a separately implemented recursive oracle across all 626 binary-tree shapes with zero through seven nodes, once with unique values and once with duplicate values.

A separate 30,000-node right-skewed tree completes through the actual iterative candidate and yields the expected preorder/inorder ascending sequence and postorder descending sequence, exercising the non-recursive depth boundary.
The O(n) time and O(h) auxiliary-stack claims are consistent with the implementations; the answer correctly distinguishes stack auxiliary space from the O(n) output list.
Morris traversal is identified as a different answer-side tradeoff because it can reduce auxiliary space by temporarily modifying tree links; it is not incorrectly asserted as a source requirement.
